sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Gaurav Kakkar,Rama Shankar Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- Amit Saxena Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.

Heard Mr. Pawan Giri, learned counsel for the applicants, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State of U.P./opposite party No.1, Mr. Amit Saxena, learned counsel for opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants, namely, Yogesh, Sunil,
Smt. Usha Devi and Manorma to quash the charge-sheet dated 30.12.2012 and entire proceedings of Case No. 546 of 2013 arising out of Case Crime No. 529 of 2012, under Section 498-A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Bulandshahr presently pending in the Court of learned Civil Judge, Junior Division-II, FTC, Bulandshahr on the Yogesh And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58595940/
1 basis of compromise between the parties concerned.
Filtering out unnecessary details, the basic facts in brief, which are necessary for disposal of this case as argued by the learned counsel for the applicants are that the applicants are husband,
father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law of opposite party no. 2.
This is a matrimonial dispute between applicant no. 1 and daughter of opposite party no.2.

Marriage of applicant no. 1 was solemnized on 11.05.2011 with the daughter of opposite party no. 2, but on account of matrimonial dispute between them, opposite party no. 2 lodged F.I.R. on 14.08.2012 against the applicants for the alleged offence under Sections 498A, 323, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act making allegation inter alia of harassment of his daughter in her matrimonial home, in which after culmination of investigation, charge-sheet has been submitted against them on 30.12.2012, on which the concerned Court took cognizance on 17.04.2013 and summoned the applicants to face trial.
Vide order dated 11.07.2023, interim protection was granted to the applicants that no coercive action shall be taken against them.

It is pointed out by learned counsel for the applicants that during pendency of this application before this Court, applicant no. 1 Yogesh Kumar and his wife Smt. Kalpana (daughter of opposite party no. 2) entered into a compromise and they filed a petition for dissolution of marriage by decree of divorce under Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Karkarduma, Delhi which was registered as HMA No. 601 of 2017 on 14.10.2017.

entities.text: Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Karkarduma, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said divorce petition was allowed vide order dated 24.10.2017 and marriage between the applicant no. 1 and daughter of opposite party no. 2 dissolved through a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

It is further submitted that as per the terms of settlement, total a sum of Rs. 9 lacs towards maintenance, dowry articles and alimony, etc. was to be paid by the applicant no. 1 to Smt.
Kalpana (daughter of opposite party no. 2) and accordingly, applicant no. 1 has paid a sum of Rs. 3 lacs, Rs. 2 lacs and Rs. 1.5 lacs on 30.03.2017, 20.10.2017 and 05.10.2024, respectively.

So far as remaining amount of Rs. 2.5 lacs is concerned, learned counsel for the applicants produced a draft no. 000149 dated 02.12.2024 of Rs. 2.5 lacs in favour of Smt. Kalpana (daughter of opposite party no. 2).
The original draft is handed over to Smt. Kalpana by applicant no. 1, who are present in person before this Court.

On the strength of aforesaid facts, it is submitted that on account of compromise arrived at between the parties concerned, all disputes between them have come to an end, therefore, aforesaid criminal proceeding against the applicants is liable to be quashed by this Court.
Learned Additional Government Advocate and learned counsel appearing on behalf of opposite party no.2 do not dispute the aforesaid facts.

Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 has also submitted at the Bar that since the parties concerned have settled their dispute as mentioned above,
therefore, opposite party no.2 does not want to prosecute the applicants and has no objection in quashing the impugned criminal proceedings against the applicants.

sentences.text: 2 Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, I find that after settlement arrived at between the parties in the present case, the chance of ultimate conviction is bleak and, therefore, no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution against the applicants to continue, as the same would be a futile exercise and a sheer wastage of precious time of the Court.
The continuation of a criminal proceedings after compromise would cause oppression and prejudice to the parties concerned.

If the parties concerned want to bury the hatchet and are willing to move on in a matrimonial dispute on the basis of compromise, they may be allowed to compound the offences in terms of settlement, because in such circumstances the proceedings can hardly be taken to their logical culmination and, the prospect of conviction gets lost.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case in the light of dictum and guidelines laid down by the Apex Court in case of B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 1 SCC (Cri) 848 and State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296, this Court feels that this is a fit case, where this Court can exercise its inherent power to secure the ends of justice.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case in hand interest of justice would be met, if the prayer of parties is acceded to and the criminal proceedings and other litigation between the parties are brought to an end.

In view of the above, impugned charge-sheet dated 30.12.2012 and entire proceedings of Case No.
546 of 2013 against the applicants are hereby quashed.
In the conspectus of the aforesaid, this application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed in terms of compromise as mentioned above.
